task.title: Desktop: run tracking, delivery on idle, run card and replay
task.description: Keryx Desktop web view (apps/desktop/src). Make a Run click a tracked run whose result goes back to the session that showed the button, per plan.md ("Chosen approach", "Wire contract", "State × event matrix"). Already built and committed: host commands via `ptyOpenCommand(cwd, command, title, cols, rows)` and `ptyTail(id, lines)` in `apps/desktop/src/platform/panels.ts` (T5; exit arrives as `onPtyExit` → `panel://pty-exit {id, code}`), and the keryx server side (T6: `src/acp/terminal-result.ts`, `src/acp/server.ts` `terminalResultsOf`, `src/acp/profile.ts:148-172`). WHAT TO BUILD: (1) `runInTerminal` (apps/desktop/src/panels/panelBus.ts) carries an optional origin `{ sessionId, source: "message" | "tool" }`; both Run buttons pass it — the message code block (components/Markdown.tsx onClick, a module-level handler: give it the session through a prop or React context set by the transcript; Markdown rendered outside a session — wiki pages, PR text — has no origin) and the tool card (session/Transcript.tsx:200-204). (2) TerminalPanel's run request opens a NEW tab with `ptyOpenCommand` in the project root (title = the command, shortened) and never writes into the active tab; a start failure keeps the existing "Could not run the command" toast. A run without an origin is just that tab: no tracking, no card, nothing sent. (3) A run store (new `apps/desktop/src/session/terminalRuns.ts`, pure logic separated from React so it is unit-testable; model it on `session/delegateTerminals.ts`) keyed by runId (generate one matching /^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,64}$/) with sessionId, command, tabId, startedAt and state: starting | running | waiting (finished, session busy) | sent | sent-while-running | closed | start-failed | not-sent (keryx too old). On `onPtyExit` for the run's tab: `ptyTail(tabId, 200)`, keep at most the LAST 16 KiB of UTF-8 bytes, build the result. If the user closed the tab first (panelBus `notifyTabClosed`/`onTabClosed`) the run is `closed` and nothing is sent — the exit event that follows a close must not turn it into a result. portable-pty reports a signal-killed process as code 1 and never null, so do not rely on `code: null` (pass whatever code arrives; null stays possible on the wire). (4) Delivery: send only when `initialize._meta.keryx.terminalResults === true` (read it where useAcpSession reads `initialize._meta.keryx.extensions`, ~:99); otherwise the run becomes `not-sent` and the card says the result was not sent to the agent. Deliver to the run's own session even when another session is shown, when that session is held, initialized and has no turn running (the conditions `sendPrompt` checks at useAcpSession.ts:376-422); otherwise mark `waiting` and retry when that session's turn ends (`busy` → false) or it becomes held again. Everything waiting for one session goes in ONE `session/prompt` (at most 8 per prompt; more → the next prompt after that turn ends). The prompt: `{ sessionId, prompt: [{ type: "text", text: <a short display line> }], _meta: { keryx: { terminalResults: [...] } } }` where each entry has EXACTLY the six fields `runId`, `command`, `state`, `exitCode`, `durationMs`, `output` — `exitCode` only when `state` is "exited", never on "running"; each runId once per prompt; never combined with `issueLaunchId`/`resumeIssueQuestions` (the server refuses all of these as invalid params — owner decision: strict). keryx ignores the display text and writes its own continuation line, so the transcript must NOT draw that send as a user bubble: the run card switches to sent and the agent's reply streams as usual. A busy refusal (`condition: session-busy`) puts the results back to waiting. (5) "Send output now" on a running run: `ptyTail` now, send one snapshot (`state: "running"`, no exitCode) the same way, state `sent-while-running`; the later exit only updates the card (exit code shown) and is never sent again. (6) The run card in the transcript (a new transcript item in session/reducer.ts, appended when the run starts, next to how the `delegateResult` card is added at reducer.ts:514-515/636; style it with the existing tokens, e.g. styles/delegate.css as the model): the command, the state in words (running…, waiting for the agent's turn to end, sent to the agent, closed before it finished, could not start: <error>, not sent: this keryx does not take run results), the exit code with ok/failed styling, the duration, a collapsible output tail, "Show tab" (panelBus `showTerminalTab`) while the tab exists, and "Send output now" while running and not yet sent. (7) Replay on session/load: a user chunk with `_meta.keryx.terminalResult` ({runId, command, state, exitCode?, durationMs, output}) is drawn as a run card in the sent state (no actions), and a user chunk with `_meta.keryx.terminalContinuation: true` draws nothing — mirror reducer.ts:287-289 for `delegateResult`. No turn starts on replay. Runs are not persisted across a window reload (an undelivered run is simply gone). Write the tests first (tdd-workflow): `apps/desktop/src/session/terminalRuns.test.ts` (store and delivery logic: exit → one prompt with exact fields and caps; busy → waiting → one prompt for several results; another session shown; closed before exit sends nothing even when an exit event follows; start failure; keryx without terminalResults; send-now then exit is not resent; more than 8 waiting), `apps/desktop/src/session/terminalRun*.dom.test.tsx` (the card's states and actions, replay of the two meta chunks, no user bubble), and update `apps/desktop/src/panels/RunButton.dom.test.tsx` plus any existing test that expected Run to type into the active tab (e.g. panels/SidePanels.dom.test.tsx) to the new behaviour: Run opens its own tab via ptyOpenCommand and the active tab gets no write.

acceptance_criteria: AC1: Run on a single-command shell block in a message and Run on an executed `execute` tool card both open a new terminal tab whose process is the user's login shell running exactly that command (`pty_open_command`); the previously active tab receives no input. [verify: exec `bun --cwd apps/desktop test src/panels/RunButton`]

AC3: When the run's process exits, the session that showed the Run button — also while another session is shown — receives exactly one `session/prompt` whose `_meta.keryx.terminalResults` carries that run's `runId`, `command`, `state: "exited"`, `exitCode`, `durationMs` and at most 200 lines / 16 KiB of plain-text output, and a follow-up agent turn starts with no user input. [verify: exec `bun --cwd apps/desktop test src/session/terminalRun`]

AC4: A result whose process ends while that session's turn is running waits and is delivered when the turn ends; results that waited together are delivered in one `session/prompt` (one follow-up turn). [verify: exec `bun --cwd apps/desktop test src/session/terminalRun`]

AC7 (client half): After `session/load`, keryx replays each stored note as a user chunk with `_meta.keryx.terminalResult` (the parsed fields, never the envelope) and the continuation line with `_meta.keryx.terminalContinuation: true`; the desktop draws the note as a run card (command, exit code, output) and draws no user bubble for the continuation line; no turn starts. [verify: exec `bun test src/acp/terminal-result && bun --cwd apps/desktop test src/session/terminalRun`]

AC8: Failure paths send nothing to the agent and start no turn: closing the run tab before the command ends kills it and the card says it was closed before it finished; a shell that cannot start shows the "Could not run the command" toast and a card naming the error; a keryx whose `initialize` lacks `_meta.keryx.terminalResults` gets no prompt and the card says the result was not sent. [verify: exec `bun --cwd apps/desktop test src/session/terminalRun src/panels/RunButton` · sensitive: failure-scenario]

AC9: "Send output now" on a running run delivers one snapshot (`state: "running"`, no `exitCode`) and starts a follow-up turn; the run's later exit updates the card and is not delivered again. [verify: exec `bun --cwd apps/desktop test src/session/terminalRun`]

Agent conduct (mandatory): (1) No AI attribution: no `Co-Authored-By:` trailer or "Generated by/with …" line naming an AI model, agent or tool in commit messages, PR or ticket descriptions, or comments. A human co-author, a code-generator note and a model name as technical provenance are allowed. (2) No commit, push, merge or release without an explicit ask. Invoking an orchestrator is the ask for its own task-boundary commits; merge and release always need their own ask. (3) Never destroy others' work: no `git stash` in a dirty tree, no blanket `git add -A` while parallel lanes share a checkout, no force-push to a shared branch. (4) No secrets or personal data in output, logs or commits. (5) Report honestly: name what failed, what was skipped and what was not verified.
Follow rules/process/git-concurrency.mdc: never git stash; never git add -A.
